title: C482/338/2009 of SMT. SONU MISHRA AND ANR Vs STATE AND ANR

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No. 338 of 2009
(Under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.)
Smt. Sonu Mishra and another .......... Applicants
versus
State of Uttarakhand & another ....... Respondents
Mr. Shailendra Singh Chauhan, Advocate, present for the petitioners-applicants.
Smt. P.S.Soun, A.G.A, assisted by Ms. Meena Bohara, present for the
State/respondent no. 1.
U.C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
1. The applicants Smt. Sonu Mishra and Dileep Mishra, by
means of present petition moved under Section 482 Cr.
P.C., seek to quash the charge-sheet dated 19.08.2007,
summoning order dated 13.11.2007 and the entire criminal
proceedings of Criminal Case No. 643 of 2007 captioned as
State vs. Dileep Mishra and another, in respect of offences
punishable under Sections 498-A, 323, 506 of I.P.C.,
pending in the Court of Judicial Magistrate, Ranikhet,
District Almora.
2. Informant (respondent no. 2 herein) lodged a first
information report against the accused persons (applicants
herein) at PS Ranikhet, which was registered as case crime
no. 322 of 2007 under Sections 498-A, 323 and 506 IPC.
After the investigation, a charge-sheet was submitted
against the accused-applicants for the selfsame offences.

2
Cognizance was taken by the learned Magistrate. Accused
persons were summoned to face the trial. Aggrieved
against the same, present application under Section 482
Cr.P.C. was moved.
3. Application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. was dismissed for
want of prosecution on 30.05.2013. Thereafter, on an
application moved on behalf of the applicants, the petition
was restored to it's original number along with interim
order vide order dated 11.07.2013. Respondent no.2 was
directed to be issued notice. The same was issued. The
registry has indicated vide endorsement dated 07.08.2013
that notice was personally served upon the respondent no.
2. None has appeared for her in the Court. No counter
affidavit was filed by the respondent no. 2 before dismissal
of the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
4. Learned counsel for the applicants stated that the parties
have settled their disputes amicably.
5. An affidavit is filed by the applicant no. 2 along with Misc.
Application CRMA No. 1792 of 2013 to emphasize that
since the parties have buried their differences amicably,
therefore, the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. be
decided in terms of compromise. It will be useful to
reproduce paragraphs 3, 4 & 5 of the affidavit herein
below:
 "A separate complaint case no. 323 of 2007
was filed by respondent no. 2 Vineeta in the Court of
Judicial Magistrate, Ranikhet, district Almora against
as many as seven persons. In the aforesaid case, a
cognizance order was passed on 04.08.2007 against all

3
the accused persons under Sections 323, 420, 504,
493, 595 and 109 of IPC. In the aforesaid case, a
compounding application was filed in the criminal
application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No. 323 of 2007
before this Hon'ble Court which was numbered as
1373 of 2012. Aforesaid application was allowed by
this Hon'ble Court vide order dated 31.12.2012. The
applicants could not file compounding application in
the instant matter because in both the cases the
counsels of applicants were different and he was under
impression that both the cases are quashed, but when
this petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. was dismissed
for want of prosecution vide order dated 30.05.2013,
only then petitioner came to know about the pendency
of this petition.
 The petitioners moved recall application
dated 09.07.2013 for the recall application of the order
dated 30.05.2013 which was allowed and the
proceeding of the instant case no. 322 of 2007 under
Sections 323, 506 and 498-A IPC was stayed by this
Hon'ble Court and fresh notice was issued to
respondent no. 2. The matter has already been
amicably settled between the parties. The respondent
no. 2 is not appearing due to the reason best known to
her"
6. Copy of the order dated 31.12.2012 passed by this Court in
C-482 Petition No. 1373 of 2012 was also filed. The
relevant portion of the order is being reproduced herein
below :
 "Learned counsel for the parties have
apprised this Court that trial has still not
commenced and parties have entered into a
compromise.
 Ms. Vinita informed this Court that she has
received all her dues from Delip Mishra, with whom

4
she married under the impression that he was a
bachelor.
 In the above faces and circumstances,
compounding application is allowed. Impugned order
of cognizance and entire proceedings of criminal case
no. 323 of 2007 pending in the court of Judicial
Magistrate, Ranikhet, District Almora are hereby
quashed.
 This petition stands disposed of."
7. There is, therefore, no reason to disbelieve the statement of
learned counsel for the applicants that the parties have
settled their disputes amicably outside the Court. None has
appeared for the respondent no. 2 to deny such fact.
8. Accused-applicants were summoned to face the trial for the
offences punishable under Sections 323, 506 and 498-A
IPC. Whereas offences punishable under Sections 323 and
506 IPC are compoundable offences within the scheme of
Section 320 Cr.P.C., offence under Section 498-A IPC is
not. The question is- whether the respondent no. 2 should
be permitted to compound such offences against the
applicants are not?
9. Learned counsel for the applicants drew the attention of
this Court towards the ruling of Gian Singh v. State of
Punjab and another (2013) 1 SCC (Cri) 160 in which
Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as below:
"The position that emerges from the above
discussion can be summarised thus: the power of
the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding
or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent
jurisdiction is distinct and different from the
power given to a criminal court for compounding
the offences under Section 320 of the Code.

5
Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no
statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in
accord with the guideline engrafted in such power
viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to
prevent abuse of the process of any Court. In what
cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or
complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the
offender and victim have settled their dispute
would depend on the facts and circumstances of
each case and no category can be prescribed.
However, before exercise of such power, the High
Court must have due regard to the nature and
gravity of the crime. Heinous and serious offences
of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape,
dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even
though the victim or victim's family and the
offender have settled the dispute. Such offences
are not private in nature and have serious impact
on society. Similarly, any compromise between the
victim and offender in relation to the offences
under special statutes like Prevention of
Corruption Act or the offences committed by
public servants while working in that capacity etc;
cannot provide for any basis for quashing criminal
proceedings involving such offences. But the
criminal cases having overwhelmingly and pre-dominatingly civil flavour stand on different
footing for the purposes of quashing, particularly
the offences arising from commercial, financial,
mercantile, civil, partnership or such like
transactions or the offences arising out of
matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family
disputes where the wrong is basically private or
personal in nature and the parties have resolved
their entire dispute. In this category of cases, High
Court may quash criminal proceedings if in its
view, because of the compromise between the
offender and victim, the possibility of conviction is
remote and bleak and continuation of criminal
case would put accused to great oppression and
prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused
to him by not quashing the criminal case despite
full and complete settlement and compromise with
the victim. In other words, the High Court must
consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to
the interest of justice to continue with the
criminal proceeding or continuation of the
criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of
process of law despite settlement and compromise
between the victim and wrongdoer and whether to
secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that
criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to
the above question(s) is in affirmative, the High

6
Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash
the criminal proceeding."
10. The instant case is squarely covered by the said ruling of
the Hon'ble Supreme Court. The reply to the question
posed above is in the affirmative in view of the rulings of
Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S.Joshi's case, (2003) 4 SCC
675 and Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and another
(2013) 1 SCC (Cri) 160.
11. As a consequence thereof, application under Section 482
Cr.P.C. is allowed on the basis of compromise arrived at
between the parties. The charge-sheet dated 19.08.2007,
summoning order dated 13.11.2007 and the entire criminal
proceedings of Criminal Case No. 643 of 2007 captioned as
State vs. Dileep Mishra and another, in respect of offences
punishable under Sections 498-A, 323, 506 of I.P.C.,
pending in the Court of Judicial Magistrate, Ranikhet,
District Almora is hereby quashed. CRMA No. 1792 of
2013 are accordingly disposed of.
 (U.C. Dhyani, J.)
Dated :22.11.2013
Kaushal
